newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU urged to promote cross-border study, training.
newsitem.headline: EU urged to promote cross-border study, training.

text.p: The European Union must do more to smoothe the way for citizens to study, get training and conduct research in other EU countries, the European Commission said on Wednesday.
"There remain a large number of completely discouraging barriers to facilitating this mobility," Education Commissioner Edith Cresson told a news conference.

The Commission adopted a Green Paper, or discussion document, outlining a range of initiatives that the EU should consider taking to remove legal and financial obstacles to cross-border study and research.
As an example, it said that unemployed people who want training in another EU state lose their jobless benefits if they are gone for more than three months.

Young graduates who seek training across borders may also face problems with residency rights or lose their social security coverage because they are not technically either students or employees, it added.

The Commission's paper includes proposals that the EU consider creating an EU legal framework for internships and volunteer work, common conditions for research grantholders and a guarantee that trainees are covered by national social security schemes.
